hunks.sol: “Young Hero Gung, doesn’t the Captain seem unusually talkative today?”

hunks.sol: “Hmm. Normally, the Captain’s hands would move before his mouth. But now he’s trying to talk his way out of it? There’s definitely something going on.”

hunks.baseline: “Absolutely. Do you think I’ve only been beaten once or twice? There’s a reason and a flow to all this.”
hunks.sol: “Absolutely. Do you think I’ve only been beaten once or twice? There’s a logic and flow to these things.”

hunks.sol: As Hyuk Mujin stared at me through narrowed eyes, Gung Gibang’s eyes suddenly widened, and he glanced around.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, yeah. He was with us a moment ago. Where the hell did he go?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, you’re right. He was here a moment ago. Where the hell did he go?”

hunks.baseline: Where did he go? He had already gone outside to wait for me.
hunks.sol: Where else? He was already outside waiting for me.

hunks.sol: Outside, Mungyeong stood waiting in the courtyard, dressed in spotless white robes.

hunks.baseline: The pressure of that endless repetition was no joke. His aura was being directed at me so subtly that no one else could notice it, and I swallowed hard.
hunks.sol: The pressure of that broken-record routine was no joke. His aura bore down on me so subtly that no one else could detect it, and I swallowed hard.

hunks.baseline: Was he this year’s actor selected by the Cannes Film Festival?
hunks.sol: Had Cannes named him Actor of the Year or something?

hunks.baseline: He blinked as if he truly knew nothing. For an instant, even I almost fell for it.
hunks.sol: He blinked as if he truly had no idea what I was talking about. For a moment, even I nearly fell for it.

hunks.baseline: The monster wearing the shell of a young medical apprentice smiled brightly and continued.
hunks.sol: The monster wearing the skin of a young medical apprentice smiled brightly and continued.

hunks.baseline: Holding back tears, I began walking after Mungyeong.
hunks.sol: Holding back tears, I followed Mungyeong.

hunks.baseline: We avoided the occasional disciples of the Zhuge Clan and Wudang, along with the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold, and entered a deserted area. Only then did Mungyeong finally speak.
hunks.sol: We avoided the occasional disciples of the Zhuge Clan and Wudang, along with the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold, until we reached a deserted area. Only then did Mungyeong finally speak.

hunks.baseline: “Dark Heaven. Did they do this?”
hunks.sol: “Dark Heaven. Was this their doing?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. It seems that way.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. It looks that way.”

hunks.baseline: “It seems that way, sir.”
hunks.sol: “It appears so, sir.”

hunks.baseline: “So it is not certain yet.”
hunks.sol: “So you are not certain yet.”

hunks.baseline: “There is always a possibility. But even though no formation was found, I believe this was definitely Dark Heaven’s doing.”
hunks.sol: “There is always some possibility of error. But although we haven’t found the formation, I’m convinced Dark Heaven was responsible.”

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong muttered the words under his breath, then suddenly raised his head.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong murmured the words, then raised his head.

hunks.baseline: He silently stared at the dark night sky, where even the full moon had hidden itself. After a moment, he spoke without warning.
hunks.sol: He silently gazed at the dark night sky, where even the full moon had hidden itself. After a moment, he abruptly asked, “Did you notice anything strange about the corpses?”

hunks.baseline: “Did you notice anything strange when looking at the corpses?”
“The marks left on them.”
hunks.sol: “The wounds left on them.”

hunks.baseline: Every death left traces. This was especially true of deaths caused by fighting between martial artists.
hunks.sol: Every death left traces. This was especially true of deaths caused by battles between martial artists.

hunks.baseline: I had heard that a master with broad experience and a deep understanding of various martial arts could identify an opponent’s weapon and even determine which form had killed the deceased simply by examining the wounds left on the corpse.
hunks.sol: I had heard that a widely experienced master with a deep understanding of various martial arts could identify the weapon used—and even determine which form had killed the victim—simply by examining the wounds on a corpse.

hunks.baseline: And the young medical apprentice before me possessed the insight and martial arts to make him one of the finest forensic examiners in Murim.
hunks.sol: And the young medical apprentice before me possessed both the discernment and martial prowess to make him one of the finest examiners of the dead in Murim.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve never seen wounds like these before. They seem to follow the principles of the very basic Three Calamities Sword Technique, yet they ripple like waves. They’re extremely strange and unusual.”
hunks.sol: “I have never seen wounds like these before. They seem to follow the principles of the very basic Three Calamities Sword Technique, yet they undulate like waves. They are exceedingly strange.”

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong slowly raised one hand and waved it through the air. Strands of internal energy flowed from his fingertips, giving off a faint light in the darkness.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong slowly raised one hand and swept it through the air. Thread-thin strands of internal energy flowed from it, glowing faintly in the darkness.

hunks.baseline: “If I had to guess, the culprit was not using an ordinary weapon. It was an unusual weapon with a crooked blade, something resembling a Snake Sword.”
hunks.sol: “If I had to guess, the culprit did not use an ordinary weapon. It was an unusual weapon with a winding blade, something akin to a Snake Sword.”

hunks.baseline: “I thought they were cut with Force.”
hunks.sol: “I thought they’d been cut with Force.”

hunks.baseline: “Your guess is correct. It was Force—or something equally sharp.”
hunks.sol: “Your guess is correct. It was Force—or something every bit as sharp.”

hunks.baseline: And no matter how thoroughly Dark Heaven had prepared, there was no way all those soldiers could have been equipped with weapons made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
hunks.sol: And no matter how thoroughly Dark Heaven had prepared, there was no way so many of its forces could have been armed with weapons made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

hunks.baseline: This was not a matter of capital. It was a matter of resource scarcity.
hunks.sol: This was not a question of capital. It was a question of resource scarcity.

hunks.baseline: As I stood lost in thought, Mungyeong asked me a question.
hunks.sol: As I stood lost in thought, Mungyeong asked, “Did you examine all the corpses?”

hunks.baseline: “Did you examine all the corpses?”
“Not all of them. I looked at the ones that stood out. I’m not especially knowledgeable, so even after seeing them firsthand, I couldn’t tell what martial arts or forms had been used.”
hunks.sol: “Not all of them. I looked at the ones that stood out. I’m not particularly knowledgeable, so even after examining them myself, I couldn’t tell which martial arts or forms had been used.”

hunks.baseline: “Among the corpses you examined was that of Hwang Chung, the Yangtze One Saber. What did you think?”
hunks.sol: “One of the corpses you examined belonged to Hwang Chung, the Yangtze One Saber. What did you make of it?”

hunks.baseline: “His waist was severed in a single blow by Force. But the decay was so severe that I couldn’t determine anything beyond that…”
hunks.sol: “He’d been cut cleanly in two at the waist by Force. But the decay was so severe that I couldn’t determine anything beyond that…”

hunks.baseline: “What about the Mad Water Saber Demon and the Wave Fox?”
hunks.sol: “And the Mad Water Saber Demon and the Wave Fox?”

hunks.baseline: A common feature shared by three corpses had just come to mind.
hunks.sol: A detail shared by all three corpses had just occurred to me.

hunks.baseline: I had seen several corpses like that earlier, so I had not found it strange at the time. But now that I thought about it, it was certainly suspicious.
hunks.sol: I had seen several other corpses like that, so it had not struck me as strange at the time. Now that I thought about it, though, it was certainly suspicious.

hunks.baseline: “Wasn’t it because the fish ate them?”
hunks.sol: “Didn’t the fish eat them?”

hunks.baseline: “That would not be entirely incorrect. According to my examination, the massacre at Donghu Stronghold took place ten days ago. The cold weather ended long ago, so severe decay is only natural. The corpses that were submerged in water would be even worse.”
hunks.sol: “That would not be entirely wrong. From what I determined, the massacre at Donghu Stronghold took place ten days ago. The cold has been gone for some time, so severe decay is only natural. The corpses submerged in water would have fared even worse.”

hunks.baseline: “Compared to them, the limbs of the commoners’ corpses were relatively intact. Did you notice that?”
hunks.sol: “By comparison, the commoners’ corpses still had their limbs relatively intact. Did you notice that?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. Those who had not learned martial arts were not cut apart. They had been crushed.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Those who hadn’t learned martial arts weren’t cut apart. They were crushed.”

hunks.baseline: Unlike the corpses of the river bandits, the bodies of the children, women, and elderly had not been severed. Their entire bodies had simply been crushed and pulverized.
hunks.sol: Unlike the river bandits’ corpses, the bodies of the children, women, and elderly had not been severed. Their entire bodies had simply been crushed and mangled.

hunks.baseline: “The houses and the ground around them had all collapsed. That would have been impossible without a force of ten thousand geun, and it is not a method an internal-arts master with powerful internal energy would choose.”
hunks.sol: “The houses and the surrounding ground had caved in everywhere. That would have been impossible without a force of ten thousand geun, and it is not a method an internal-arts master with profound internal energy would choose.”

hunks.baseline: “…I was just talking to myself.”
hunks.sol: “…I was talking to myself.”

hunks.baseline: He was being awfully sensitive.
hunks.sol: He was awfully sensitive about this.

hunks.baseline: After making that hasty excuse, I fell silent for a moment.
hunks.sol: After hurriedly making that excuse, I fell silent and considered the matter.

hunks.sol: Internal arts emphasized the efficient use and application of internal energy. External arts also used internal energy, but focused on tempering the body to its absolute limits.

hunks.sol: “There are two?”

hunks.sol: “I would estimate that they are at least as formidable as the Qilian Three Fiends we faced in Sichuan. And at least one of them uses an unusual weapon.”

hunks.baseline: “With this much information, the Third Fiend might know something. He must have heard who his fellow conspirators were.”
hunks.sol: “With this much information, the Third Fiend might know something. He must have at least heard who his comrades were.”

hunks.sol: The Third Fiend we had captured in Sichuan was one of the reasons I was going to the Zhuge Clan.

hunks.baseline: *Perhaps we can even use him to find the formation.*
hunks.sol: *Maybe we can even put him out front and have him lead us to the formation.*

hunks.baseline: It took me a long time to understand what he meant.
hunks.sol: It took me quite a while to grasp what he meant.

hunks.baseline: The shock felt as if someone had struck me in the back of the head with a hammer.
hunks.sol: The realization struck like a hammer to the back of my head.

hunks.baseline: “An experienced Supreme Peak master. Forms and wounds so unusual that it is difficult to read them. There are not many people who have reached that realm and use a weapon like this.”
hunks.sol: “A seasoned Supreme Peak master. Forms and wounds so unusual that they are difficult to read. There cannot be many people at that realm who wield such a weapon.”

hunks.sol: A dry voice emerged from between Mungyeong’s lips.

hunks.sol: “The Dongting Fisherman. For now, he is the most likely suspect.”

hunks.sol: The eccentric master who had never left the area around Dongting Lake in his entire life.

hunks.sol: A Supreme Peak master who, unusually, used a fishing rod made of black wood as his signature weapon. Enraged by the tragic news concerning his friend, the head of the Sea Serpent Society, he had crossed Tianling Falls and disappeared.
